features.label: Chat with streamed replies
features.description: The main conversation view: send a message, watch the reply stream in, with attachments and artifacts beside it.

decisions.note: Resting orb sits under the last message on every surface (ai #357).

Polish pass from three reference shots: card-in-tray composer, numbered question card, working pill and shaped placeholders, one PreviewCard for every grid, Reply tray (the quote travels in the message text). Composer images now reach the model as file parts via `attachments` on /agent-chat and /ai/chat; before, they were never sent. Eoj: cards below the box on Desktop, previews above it on phone; neutral beam, never tan; full-colour logos.

Any file or folder can be attached (no allow-list; text sniffed by content). Cards appear at once with Reading…; video/audio/other files go as Allternit Cloud links; sent messages show chips, not extracted text. Eoj: no grey ring on the composer; the tray only shows behind a reply strip or attachment cards.

features.label: Interactive answers
features.description: Assistant replies can include an interactive card written in OpenUI Lang inside an openui code fence: metrics, tables, charts, steps and inputs that recompute on the page; buttons and choices send a follow-up message; Query()/Mutation() read and (with an Allow each time) change data through the user's MCP connectors. The app sends the model manual with every chat turn unless Settings says Text only; channels get the card as readable text.

decisions.note: Renderer shipped on the polish primitives, with deterministic local state via OpenUI $state and no eval. The model-side prompt is a separate session by Eoj's call: no per-model testing, no training.

The app (not gizzi-code) sends the manual as systemPrompt / '+' system, so each build only asks for components it renders and the TUI and channels never get it. Settings → Response style → Layout and visuals (Auto / Text only) is per device, like the Memory switches, to avoid a manual prod migration.

Live data through the MCP Apps bridge: Query() only on read-only tools, writes only as a Mutation() from a button with an Allow bar every time. OpenUI Gateway and observability-cloud are not used (owned infra; no data to Thesys). react-lang pinned to 0.3.1 to respect pnpm's minimum release age.

Removed the [v:...] pseudo-syntax, AllternitOpenUIRenderer/registry, BlueprintCanvas, the test-only code-compiler and the fake render_walkthrough tool. Design mode previews the reply's card with DESIGN.md tokens; UI Forge is the card playground.

features.label: Bot Mode threads and templates
features.description: Each bot keeps its own threads, starts from a template, and shows where a message came from.

decisions.note: Bot templates shipped and the old Bot Hub was removed (ai #209, #210).

features.label: Bots on every channel
features.description: One bot reachable by email, SMS, phone, WhatsApp, Teams, Slack, Discord and Telegram, with the same identity everywhere.

decisions.note: Teams and WhatsApp Business connect merged (platform #1340, ai #441).
Texts only go to people who texted first; contacts and invites get calls only (platform #1343).
Bot email on customer domains runs through mx.allternit.com on the standby server, not the prod VPS.

features.label: Your digital twin
features.description: A bot that acts as you across channels, with its own view of what it handled and what needs you.

features.label: Factory teams and panes
features.description: Start agents and teams, watch their panes live, and approve their work, locally or on another computer.

decisions.note: Remote panes (platform #1396) and Factory on cloud computers (#1397) merged and deployed.
Save as template and a team picker added; m.allternit.com redeployed with them.
Remote bots are mirrored over the peer port instead of a Mesh pane endpoint, so the other computer's pane shell is not exposed.

features.label: Memory Drive
features.description: Agent memory as a drive: notes, retrieval and nightly consolidation shared by bots, the workspace and gizzi.

decisions.note: All phases merged (platform #1348, #1362; ai #445, #448).
Computer sync runs inside the Desktop app, two-way, with no main copy.

features.label: Voice in and out
features.description: Talk to agents by voice on any device, with a full-screen orb mode and an in-session call bar.

decisions.note: Light-standard plan approved: speech runs in the Rust voice service on any device; cloud voice runs on the standby server.
Cloud Voice priced at $0.08 per minute, with 100 minutes in Plus.

features.label: Agents drive a computer
features.description: Agents see and drive a browser or a whole desktop, with leases and an audit trail.

decisions.note: Agent cursor overlay (computer toolset P5) in every computer viewer, from vendored MIT @trycua/cursor-motion, driven by computer.action events; style in Settings → Computers.

features.label: Cloud computers on paid plans
features.description: A paid plan provisions a hosted Linux desktop that you and your bots can view and drive from any surface.

decisions.note: Customer computers get nightly encrypted off-site backups plus owner restore points and downloads (platform #1405, ai #454).
First real Plus customer was provisioned automatically.

features.label: Cloud computer backups and restore points
features.description: Every customer cloud computer is backed up off-site each night, encrypted. Owners can take up to 5 restore points, roll back to one, and download a full copy of the computer from Settings → Computers on every surface.

decisions.note: Nightly incus-export backups to R2 on allternit-standby (8-day daily, 35-day weekly), same key scheme as the host backup; first run verified by decrypting it.
Restore points and downloads are cloud-api control-plane routes, not the computer's own runtime (which has no Incus access). Cap of 5; download links are 1-hour tokens.

features.label: Docs, Slides and Sheets
features.description: Document, slide and spreadsheet editors that agents can read and write.

features.label: MCP Apps and events
features.description: Interactive MCP apps run inside the workspace, and their events can wake a bot or ask you to approve.

decisions.note: The program ships under the name MCP Apps.
Events program live: approval_required events carry an approve link (platform #1361, ai #447).

features.label: Usage, credits and spend limits
features.description: What each account has used, what it has left, and the limits that stop runaway spend.

decisions.note: Usage dashboard added to the phone layout (ai #355).

features.label: Projects and project threads
features.description: Group chats, files and bots under a project, with its own threads and coordination.

decisions.note: Project threads match bot threads, extending the existing page instead of redesigning it (ai #358).

features.label: Cowork
features.description: Long-running work an agent carries out alongside you, with teams and preferences.

features.label: Phone layout and PWA
features.description: The same workspace sized for phones: PhoneShell on ai.allternit.com and the installable m.allternit.com app.

decisions.note: Phones get PhoneShell on ai.allternit.com (ai #341).
Every feature lands on Desktop, the ai.allternit.com phone layout and the PWA in the same change.

features.label: Platform API v1
features.description: Public developer API for accounts, messaging, numbers, channels, usage and webhooks.

decisions.note: Phases 3 to 5 deployed; P4 channels and twin merged (#1394).
Creating Stripe meters, products and prices stays a dry run until the amounts are signed off.

Launch: card required for every project (402 payment_method_required), console Billing page with Stripe Checkout (Pay as you go / Growth), webhook sets the project's customer and plan, Growth $300 credit grant per invoice, developer terms and AUP published and accepted at key creation, SDK publish workflow.

features.label: Hosted computer driver
features.description: Platform API /v1/computers: hosted computers that run a model's computer and browser tool calls, with drop-in drivers for the Anthropic SDK, OpenAI and Gemini, an MCP server, approvals and per-key limits.

decisions.note: Gated per project by hosted_driver_enabled, set by Allternit only; outside-developer computers can't reach private ranges or 169.254.169.254; pricing to be announced.

features.label: Bot avatars and photo sprites
features.description: Pick a look pack, build a character, or turn a photo into an animated bot avatar.

decisions.note: Photo avatars included with plans (Plus 5, Super 25, Ultra 50) with a $4 cost cap.

features.label: Computer toolset for every model
features.description: One contract (allternit.computer.v1 / allternit.browser.v1, Anthropic's 20260801 member sets) and one executor (POST /computers/:id/toolset) that every gizzi model adapter calls: Claude-native toolsets, OpenAI, Gemini and JSON function tools. Lease, approval, audit and coordinate scaling happen in one place.

decisions.note: Eoj: computer use works for every model. Anthropic's toolsets are absorbed as one adapter into our contract, gizzi stays the only loop, and there are no hosted third-party drivers. The old gizzi browser tool (goal-driven, a second loop) was removed in favour of the toolset browser tool.

Member gaps closed: the browser gateway runs all 31 members (refs, tabs with browser_state, console, network, JS, upload) through /v1/toolset/browser with an http(s)-only URL policy and public-only hosts for cloud targets; Windows guests run all 17 computer members through PowerShell/user32; this Mac gets cursor_position, modifier clicks and emulated mouse down/up. hold_key on macOS stays off: Cua Driver 0.34 has no hold call there. Optional browser members need an explicit enable.

features.label: Custom project and folder icons
features.description: Personal folder recipes with color, paper layers, symbols/brands, text/emoji and raster logos, shared by project and folder views. Source is implemented; installed Desktop and separate PWA releases remain pending.

decisions.note: Eoj approved the iFolder-inspired customization and requested merge/push. Recipes are personal preferences on the connected runtime; no OS icon or execution-setting changes.
Integrated with the current PreviewCard polish layout; customization stays in the card options menu. Runtime API tests are added, not locally compiled under the no-build instruction.

features.label: Artifacts (one typed store, versions, sharing)
features.description: Artifacts v2: one account-level store of typed artifacts (doc, sheet, slides, design, dashboard, motion, page, card, diagram, image, code) in cloud-api Postgres with immutable versions, view/comment/edit sharing, org admin settings and a public link route. Phase 1 server side is in; the app (ArtifactWindow, Artifacts tab) and gizzi artifact_* tools land in sibling PRs.

decisions.note: Eoj accepted the artifacts v2 contract (docs/design/artifacts-v2.md): one typed store in cloud-api under /api/v2/artifacts, private by default, links refused for artifacts that use AI or connectors, owner-only permanent delete, legacy stores import as runtime_version 1.

journeys.label: Answer with a live data card
journeys.description: From a question to a card that reads your connected app and, with your approval, changes it.

steps.says: On send, the app adds the interactive-answers manual (with your connector tools) to the turn's system prompt, unless Settings says Text only.
gizzi-code appends it to its own system prompt and the model replies with an openui fence.
The transcript splits the fence out and renders the card as it streams.
Query() runs a read-only tool through the MCP Apps bridge; a Mutation() waits for the Allow bar.
The bridge calls the connector with your own credentials and returns the result straight to the card, not the model.

journeys.label: Send a message, get a streamed reply
journeys.description: What happens between pressing send in chat and the first token appearing.

steps.says: You type in ai.allternit.com (or Desktop, or the phone layout).
The chat view sends the message.
The chat client opens the request and an event stream.
allternit-api records the turn.
allternit-api calls gizzi-code over HTTP for the model work; it never calls a provider directly.
gizzi-code routes to the chosen model provider.
Tokens stream back and render as they arrive.

journeys.label: Text your bot
journeys.description: A text to a bot's number reaches the bot on your computer and the reply goes back by SMS.

steps.says: The carrier posts the inbound text to the number's relay address.
The cloud API checks opt-in and queues the text for your runtime.
Your allternit-api picks it up from the relay.
The bot that owns the number handles it in its thread.
gizzi-code runs the bot's turn.
The reply leaves through the cloud API and the carrier.

journeys.label: Start a Factory team from your phone
journeys.description: From m.allternit.com to agents running in panes on your computer.

steps.says: You open Factory on m.allternit.com.
The phone shell shows the Factory screen.
You pick a team or template and start it.
allternit-api proxies the request to the Factory engine on that computer.
The engine starts the agents and tracks approvals.
Each agent runs in a pane you can watch live from the phone.

journeys.label: Get a cloud computer with a paid plan
journeys.description: From Stripe checkout to a desktop you can open in the workspace.

steps.says: Stripe's webhook tells the cloud API the plan is paid.
Provisioning creates the machine.
The new computer is recorded and paired to your account.
The computer boots with the Allternit runtime.
It appears in Computers, where you and your bots can open it.

journeys.label: Talk to a bot by voice
journeys.description: From pressing the mic to hearing the bot answer.

steps.says: You start voice mode.
The client picks a voice endpoint: local, or cloud with a ticket.
For cloud voice, the cloud API issues the ticket and records consent.
The voice service turns speech into text and back.
allternit-api runs the bot's turn and returns the reply to speak.

journeys.label: A bot remembers across surfaces
journeys.description: A note saved in one place is recalled by a bot somewhere else.

steps.says: You or a bot save a note to Memory Drive.
allternit-api stores it.
Nightly consolidation merges and links notes.
On a later turn, retrieval finds the relevant notes.
gizzi-code puts them in the bot's context.

journeys.label: Approve an MCP app's action
journeys.description: An app event that needs you, from the app to your approval.

steps.says: A connected MCP app sends an event.
The event feed marks it approval_required.
It lands in your Needs you inbox with an approve link.
You approve it in the workspace.
The bot it was waiting on carries on.

journeys.label: Customize a project or folder icon
journeys.description: From opening appearance controls to seeing the saved personal icon.

steps.says: Open Customize appearance from the project card options menu.
Edit folder/paper colors and the overlay; preview, save, cancel, reset or export.
Validate the recipe and send an authenticated request to the connected runtime.
Validate and persist the preference for this user; null resets it.
Refresh subscribers across the shared Desktop, web and phone UI.
